thread:
alex_h: Heads-up — ACME wants a BYO-HSM PoC but their network team says our HSM fog endpoint is blocked by their perimeter firewall. Need a short checklist and an ask for SOW timing changes.
maria_s: omg ok. do we have the exact IPs/ports they need to open?
jeff_sales: Customer provided a vendor whitelist request doc, but it lists only DNS names. they can only allow IP ranges, not hostnames.
emily_se: I can paste the minimal egress list. ports: 443 (mTLS), 22 (ops only, ephemeral), 123 (ntp). endpoints are: hsm-01.redwood-inference.net:443, hsm-02.redwood-inference.net:443. recommend they allow our NAT IP pool instead of hostnames.
alex_h: paste the NAT pool? they asked for fixed /28 for infra team.
emily_se: sure — code block inbound:
```
NAT egress CIDR: 34.210.120.0/28
Fallback NAT CIDR: 34.210.121.0/28
Required ports: 443 (mTLS), 123 (NTP), 32100-32110 (HSM backend heartbeat)
TLS: client cert required, mutual TLS with CN=x-redwood-hsm
```
jeff_sales: their security questionnaire also wants attestation docs and rotation SLA. legal_anna — can we commit to rotation window in SOW?
legal_anna: we can offer a rotation support clause but not a strict SLA for customer-managed keys in BYO HSM. propose: 30d notification window for planned rotation assistance + an optional paid 4h cutover runbook session.
maria_s: pricing question: how do we bill HSM operations during PoC? hourly support + egress?
emily_se: standard approach: include a PoC support line item (8 engineer hours/day for 5 days) + per-GB egress estimate. HSM API calls are meterless but if they want our managed key proxy there is a per-request cost.
sre_bot: incident: note — our NAT pool 34.210.120.0/28 uses AZ-a. if customer is multi-AZ make sure they also allow fallback pool 34.210.121.0/28.
alex_h: ok thanks. can someone draft a short 3-bullet SOW amendment we can push to customer? need to cover: network allowlist, 4h cutover add-on, support hours & pricing, attestation deliverables.
emily_se: drafted snippet for sales to paste:
"We will provide fixed NAT egress IP ranges (34.210.120.0/28, 34.210.121.0/28) and a mutual-TLS endpoint for HSM connections. Customer is responsible for perimeter allowlisting. Redwood will provide one 4-hour cutover assistance session as an optional add-on and a PoC support package (40 engineer-hours). Attestation artifacts (HSM vendor certs, audit logs) will be provided upon request under NDA. Additional paid support and emergency rotation assistance are scoped separately."
jeff_sales: perfect. i'll include a pricing table but quick check: do we need to mention key escrow or we simply say 'no escrow by default'?
legal_anna: state clearly: "No key escrow retained by Redwood unless explicitly agreed in SOW." adds clarity for compliance teams.
maria_s: last ask: they want a rotation dry-run during PoC to validate failover. timeline wise can we do a dry-run mid-week 3 of PoC?
emily_se: yes — schedule on week 3 with a simulated rotation (read-only traffic) and a post-run report. will need ops lead present — add 4 extra hours to PoC support line item.
alex_h: thanks team. jeff — please push amendment + pricing and flag any security questionnaire items that still need answers. i'll loop in the customer's network lead. :thumbsup:
jeff_sales: on it. pinging customer now. @maria_s i'll put the SOW snippet and pricing in the doc and leave placeholders for HSM vendor attestation files. :eyes:
